Subject: MAP kickoff — traction milestones & burst-TPM proposal

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We’re motivated to move quickly but need a MAP that lets us prove production load without committing to a full volume ladder up-front. High-level ask: a 60-day evaluation window with a single stress-test month (Black Friday window for us) where we can burst to higher TPM, followed by a staggered commit to steady-state over Q1.

Specifics we want to cover in the MAP:
- Pilot acceptance criteria (latency p95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens)
- A stress/burst month where we can scale to ~20M TPM for short windows with predictable billing
- A ramp schedule to reach ~60M TPM by the start of Jan, but with smoothing options to avoid a cliff payment in Nov
- Pricing and discount triggers tied to signed commitments and milestone acceptance

Procurement needs a draft SOW/commit schedule by Oct 15 to review with finance. I attached our internal evaluation plan for context (NovaProd_EvalPlan_v1.pdf).

Can you propose a concrete commit + ramp alternative that includes burst capacity and milestone credits?

Kate
Kate Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
NovaProd Inc

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Kate —

Appreciate the clarity and timeline. I pulled together a draft MAP that tries to balance NovaProd’s need for a high-visibility stress test with a commercially sensible commit path. Attached are two docs: Redwood_MAP_proposal.xlsx (MAP with gates) and a quick pricing snapshot (pricing_chart.png).

Summary of our proposed approach (draft):
Phase A — Pilot (30 days): baseline testing at 5M TPM cap, success gates: p95 < 350ms, error rate < 0.5%.
Phase B — Stress month (Nov): temporary burst buffer allowing peak windows up to 20M TPM. Billing model: bill at burst rate but unlock a milestone credit if acceptance gates in Phase B pass (90% of target throughput met during stress windows).
Phase C — Ramp (Dec–Jan): staged committed TPM ladder that smooths to 60M TPM by 2027-01-01. Options included:
  - Option 1 (frontloaded): 20 / 40 / 60M TPM (Dec / Jan / Feb) with 10% milestone credit applied at successful Phase B completion.
  - Option 2 (smoothed): 10 / 25 / 40 / 60M TPM across four months with a smaller initial commit but higher blended CPM—good if finance wants fewer billing surprises.

Pricing mechanics: we can provide a tiered committed rate and a burst rate (higher per-token). Credits are applied retroactively when gates are met. We also suggested a small ramp credit if NovaProd signs a 12-month committed contract after the MAP.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Review the attached MAP and indicate preferred ramp option.
2) Confirm acceptance criteria for Phase B stress windows (we can mirror your test harness metrics).
3) Ben will attach formal pricing matrix and a DocuSign-ready term sheet for procurement.

I’ll hold time next week to walk through the attachment.

—
Marissa Cole

Adding the pricing matrix and a short note on discount triggers. See pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx attached. Key commercial points:

Thanks — helpful detail. A few follow-ups from procurement/finance & engineering:

1) Smoothing preference: Finance prefers Option 2 (the smoothed 4-month ladder) to avoid a large single-month invoice in Dec. Can you produce a final blended-rate table for Option 2 that shows expected monthly spend vs committed discounts?

2) Fallout protection: We need a clearer definition of the "partial fallback credit" if Phase B fails. Procurement requests that the credit be explicitly capped (both % and dollar cap) and that we get a remediation plan tied to a 30-day extension of the pilot.

3) Contract timing: We need an SOW + term sheet to review by Oct 15 and ideally a signed agreement by Oct 31 to allow legal to run procurement checks. Any chance you can start a draft SOW now and route to our legal?

4) Burst windows: Engineering confirmed they only need the 20M TPM bursts for short 3x 2-hour windows during Black Friday. Can Redwood guarantee those windows will not be blocked by capacity? If not, what fallbacks do we have?

If you can get the updated Option 2 blended rates and the draft SOW to me by Oct 11, I’ll route to finance and legal for quick review.

-Kate

Kate —

Quick note from a legal/ops readiness perspective and a proposed compromise to address capacity guarantees and procurement timing.

Capacity guarantees: we can commit to reserved burst windows for the three 2-hour Black Friday slots, provided we reserve those slots in the Dedicated pool at signing. Operationally that looks like:
- Reserve three 2-hour burst reservations in Dedicated for Nov 26, Nov 27, Nov 29 windows (TBD exact times).
- If Redwood cannot serve the windows due to force majeure or platform outage, we will apply a 100% credit for burst fees for that affected slot.

Smoothing compromise for Option 2 (we like your finance rationale):
- Proposed ramp (smoothed): Dec: 10M TPM (committed), Jan: 25M TPM, Feb: 40M TPM, Mar: 60M TPM.
- We’ll include a 10% burst buffer above committed TPM for the first 60 days post-signature (buffer is billable at burst rate but eligible for partial credit if Phase B gates are met).

Fallback protections and caps:
- Phase B failure credit: capped at 30% of total burst fees for the month or $75k, whichever is lower.
- Pilot extension: 30 days at a reduced pilot rate (details in SOW).

Procurement timing: Ben — please convert this into the SOW language and pricing table. Kate — if we get confirmation on Option 2 by Oct 11 I’ll ask legal to prepare the term sheet and SOW for Oct 15 delivery. DocuSign link will be ready once the SOW is attached.

If that aligns I propose a short call Thursday to lock the exact burst windows and the acceptance metrics.
